newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile military brass lash out at former president.
newsitem.headline: Chile military brass lash out at former president.

text.p: Chile's military on Tuesday criticised former President Patricio Aylwin for saying he made a mistake in supporting the armed forces' coup that overthrew Marxist President Salvador Allende in 1973.
Aylwin said in a recent interview with a Mexican newspaper that he misjudged the military that ruled Chile harshly for 17 years until he was elected as president in 1990.

"We had a mistaken vision as to who the Chilean military were," Aylwin was quoted by Chilean media as telling Excelsior newspaper. "We are all guilty, we are all responsible for what happened after 1973."

Aylwin, who left office three years ago, was one of many Chilean politicians who backed the bloody coup that brought former dictator Gen. Augusto Pinochet to power. The 81-year-old general still serves as army chief.
Aylwin's comments sparked a furious reaction from army top brass, underlining the delicate relationship between Chile's civilian rulers and the powerful military.

"Ex-president of the Republic Patricio Aylwin has made declarations ... which are aggravating and highly offensive to the Chilean army and its commander-in-chief," said the statement from the corps of army generals.
It said Aylwin was making the remarks now to "justify his support for the uprising and the military government."
The military regime was notorious internationally for human rights abuses and persecution of left-wing opponents both within Chile and abroad.
